name: Naueti
confidence_why: The only statement on Naueti stress is an uncited Wikipedia sentence (penultimate, loanwords keeping their original stress) that seems to come from the author of Veloso's 2016 Leiden grammar sketch, which is closed access and has not been read, while Hull 2004 and Schapper and Huber 2023 say nothing about Naueti stress.

catalog_locator: Wikipedia 'Naueti language', section 'Vowels' (wikitext line 35); Veloso 2016 ch. 2 (unread)
catalog_quote: The vowel system is straightforward with vowels /a/, /e/, /i/, /o/ and /u/. There is no distinctive vowel length, as vowel sequences are heterosyllabic. Stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable, with very few native exceptions. Loanwords preserve their original stress.

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: the Wikipedia sentence is verbatim at wikitext line 35 of the copy consulted, and the record honestly codes 'undetermined' with an INSUFFICIENT-SOURCES flag rather than trusting it. But the deciding source is tertiary and uncited, while a 163-page 2016 Leiden grammar sketch with a phonology chapter exists and is not yet obtained; reading it would very likely change the classification from 'undetermined' to a determinate rule (probably penultimate, per the Wikipedia summary, but that cannot be asserted until ch. 2 is read). Hence at-risk in the sense that a better source likely changes the classification, with action re-read-with-listed-source = obtain Veloso 2016 (closed access; needs an author/library request). No open copy exists to download; Hull/INL 2004 (downloaded) and Schapper 2020 (held) are silent on Naueti stress; no instrumental or phonology article on Naueti was found.
